blocks.text: (RA) saying, "These have been given as gifts to me, while the others are yours." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "We have authorised your gifts for you (you may have them for yourself)." Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) then proceeded to perform his salaah and the slaves all performed salaah behind him. He then asked them, "For whom are you performing salaah?" "For Allaah," they replied. Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) said, "Then you are all for Allaah." Saying this, he set them all free.[^1]
Hadhrat Umar (RA) Donates his Land in Khaybar

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) received a piece of land in Khaybar. He then approached Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "I have received a piece of land in Khaybar. Never before have I received any property more excellent than this. What do you advise me to do with it?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "If you wish, you could make the property an endowment and donate the proceeds in charity." Hadhrat Umar (RA) therefore made the land an endowment on the condition that it should never be sold, never be given away as a gift, never be inherited and that its proceeds be given to the poor, to his relatives, to free slaves, in the path of Allaah and to guests. He also stipulated that the caretaker of the land may take from the proceeds what is normally paid and what is required to feed his guests. He however had no permission to amass wealth from it.[^2]
Hadhrat Umar (RA) Frees a Slave Woman whom he had obtained from Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA)

Hadhrat Umar (RA) once wrote to Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) to buy for him a slave woman from Jaloolaa (a place en route to Khurasan that the Muslims had conquered. Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) did as requested and sent the woman to Hadhrat Umar (RA)). Hadhrat Umar (RA) then called for her one day and said, "Allaah says (in the Qur'aan):

blocks.arabic_text: لَنْ تَنَالُوا الْبِرَّ حَتّٰى تُنْفِقُوْا مِمَّا تُحِبُّوْنَ
blocks.text: You shall never reach (true, perfect) righteousness until you spend of that which you love."[^3]
Hadhrat Umar (RA) then set her free.[^4]
The Incident of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) and a Slave Woman
Hadhrat Naafi narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) owned a slave woman. When his love for her became intense, he freed her and married her to
Haakim (Vol.3 Pg.272), narrating from reliable sources, as confirmed by Dhahabi.
Sihaah Sitta, as quoted in Nasbur Ra'yah (Vol.3 Pg.476).
Abd bin Humayd, Ibn Jareer and Ibn Mundhir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.3 Pg.314).
